overall: The Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by posting an insufficient November 6 site visit notice and by deliberating via email, but not by a pre-site-visit quorum deliberation; no intentional violation was found.

allegations.summary: Notice for the Nov 6 site visit listed 39 Gully Lane, not 35 Gully Lane where the dirt mound to be viewed was located, so the subject was not disclosed.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that although the notice for the November 6 site visit properly listed the location of the meeting it failed to reasonably advise the public of the issues to be discussed.

allegations.summary: Chair allegedly deliberated by replying by email to a resident, copying all members, and sharing his opinion of her comments on Committee business. Committee claimed cure via minutes.
allegations.key_passage: we find that Chair Sullivan improperly deliberated when he responded to the Complainant’s email, copying a quorum of the Committee, and shared his opinion about the value of the Complainant’s comments, some of which related to business within the Committee’s jurisdiction.

allegations.summary: A quorum of the Committee allegedly deliberated on Committee business informally just before convening the November 6 site visit.
allegations.key_passage: Absent sufficient evidence to support the Complainant’s allegation that a quorum of the Committee deliberated prior to convening the site visit, we credit the Committee’s account of the facts and find no violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Open Meeting Law violations were intentional.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we do not find the Committee to have intentionally violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: To the extent the complaint alleged members of the regional historic district commission deliberated improperly, the complaint was not filed with that body.
allegations.key_passage: To the extent the complaint alleges that members of the Old King’s Highway Regional Historic District Commission improperly deliberated, we decline to review this allegation where the compliant was not filed with that body.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law.
Within 30 days, amend the minutes of the January 8, 2024 meeting to include in the list of documents used at the meeting the November 6 email that constituted improper deliberation.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the Law.
